prompt:
A full-body character image, vertical 2:3 (1024×1536): Jian Yong of the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, reimagined as an adult woman — Liu Bei's oldest friend, whose jokes softened her lord's heart.

1. STYLE
Korean MMORPG character artwork. A recognisably drawn face with gently simplified anatomical structure. 2D painting with visible brushwork: layered strokes of colour, soft broken edges, thin coloured linework and a few crisp accents on the face and costume.
Her face is small and soft: a short midface, a softly rounded jaw and a small chin, about 1.3 times as long as it is wide, with her eyes open at their natural size. Bangs, side locks and headpieces frame the face without lengthening it.
Skin finish: dewy, glass-like highlights on the skin of her shoulders, arms, collarbones and legs — a soft, luminous wet-look sheen that follows the body's forms; her face keeps a soft, natural finish.

2. CHARACTER
Age: late twenties — a graceful grown-up face with soft, smooth contours.
Face — her own, recognisably this character, a woman's face with no beard or facial hair: a languid, sleepy-eyed ease; fair skin; round face; medium-sized eyes — long phoenix eyes with lifted outer corners, outer eye corners slightly lifted; thin straight brows; petite straight nose; soft, full lips; near-black obsidian eyes; a dusting of freckles across nose and cheeks.
Body and hair: slender-limbed yet full-busted with rounded hips and a narrow waist build; an elegant low chignon with no bangs, long face-framing side locks; deep wine-red hair.
Expression: a small closed-lip smile that reaches the eyes, subtle and relaxed.
Legend, carried in her design and bearing: lounging humor, loose comfortable robes, an easygoing adviser.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME AND EQUIPMENT — THREE KINGDOMS
Costume: a Han court official's dress — layered robes with a broad belt and a hanging seal cord, a black jinxian guan cap, an ink brush and bound bamboo slips. Late-Han Chinese dress — cross-collared silk robes with wide sleeves and a broad sash, lamellar or scale armor laced with cords where armor is worn, bronze, jade and lacquer ornament, Han court hair ornaments; silk, lacquered leather, bronze and iron.
Silhouette: a large phoenix crown with hanging bead strands and a weighty ceremonial robe — the headdress is the main shape. This silhouette sets the overall shape of the costume above — keep its materials, ornaments and rank in this shape; the details are free.
Colours: jade green, imperial gold, earthen brown, white jade.
Signature item: a wine gourd on a red cord. She holds it at full scale: one whole object, drawn once, held in front of or beside her body; a long weapon keeps one straight, unbroken shaft with a single head or blade.
Exposure (bold): her robes open to show skin — the cross collar opened into a deep neckline with natural cleavage, bare upper arms above detached wide sleeves (and bare shoulders where no shoulder guard sits), the skirt panels cut with a high side slit at full length — it shows the side line of one leg as she stands, no leg pushed out or knee bent for it; any armor pieces stay on and symmetrical. Intimate areas covered; keep the costume material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: Shu Han in the Sichuan basin, around 208–263 AD: the city of Chengdu, cliffside plank roads over gorges, mist-wrapped mountains and bamboo forests, peach orchards, green-and-gold banners.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: a soft key light with a strong rim light tracing her hair, shoulders and armour; bright, crisp specular highlights on metal and jewellery, and a clean, warm-neutral sheen on her skin.
Composition: her whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet inside the frame with clear margins, about four-fifths of the image height; camera at chest height with natural portrait perspective.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only — no second character, horse or other creature. No readable text or numbers, except that a banner, seal or emblem may carry the single character 蜀 or 簡. No logo, watermark, speech bubble or frame border. Three Kingdoms-era Chinese dress, architecture and materials only.
Avoid: a blue or bruise-like tint on the skin around the eyes, glossy or shiny highlights on the face, sweaty, oily or plastic-looking skin.
